# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventeen or eighteen at the time of her death  <sub>[v1 c26 P4](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0004), [v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v2 c19 P59](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0059), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal was widely considered extremely beautiful, with fair skin, large vivid blue eyes, and long, lovely yellow hair that she wore in braids. She possessed a full, eye-catching figure and a radiant complexion. During her terminal illness, she became very slender and pale, with fragile hands and a feverish flush.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Opal had a sunny, laughing, and pleasant disposition, though she was deeply preoccupied with courtship, romance, and retaining multiple male admirers. She possessed a sentimental nature and a tendency toward drama or hysterics when frightened. When faced with terminal illness, she desperately hid her fears behind a facade of continuous social activity before ultimately confessing her dread of death to Nell Harcourt.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016), [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011)_

## Goals

- To keep numerous suitors and enjoy a gay youth before settling down  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)</sub>
- To marry and have children  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>

## History

Opal attended Brierley school as a girl, where she sat in front of Hugh Carrow and frequently shared school gossip and romantic theories learned from her older sisters. She was a member of the school's Story Club under the nom-de-plume of a sentimental writer, and took part in local play-acting and concerts. Following her primary schooling, she entered the Regent's class alongside Nell Harcourt and others, going on to study at Regent's Academy in Port Marlow, where she won recognition as the most beautiful student. She subsequently secured a teaching position at Delford school. During her adolescence, she was pursued by numerous local suitors, including Nelson Atkins and Wilbur Blair, and eventually fell in love with Herb Tranter. After contracting a severe lung congestion over the winter, she developed galloping consumption, forcing her to abandon teaching. Despite maintaining an optimistic front of social outings and suitors, she privately shared her terror of dying with Nell during a conversation in her garden. She died peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter during the summer, leaving an unfinished embroidered centerpiece for Nell.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P20](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0020), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c28 P12](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0012), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c11 P8](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0008), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P33](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0033)_

## Quotes

> Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Will you come up frequently, Nell? Make sure to come by yourself—I need you.  <sub>[v3 c11 P55](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0055)</sub>

> The cemetery appears so peculiar under the moon’s light! So spectral! Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> Everyone is aware of it. It is known to me—it has been known to me the entire summer, even if I refused to admit it. And, oh, Nell—dying is not what I want. The thought of dying frightens me.  <sub>[v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live the way other girls do. I—I desire to get married, Nell—and—and—possess tiny children. You are aware that babies were always something I loved, Nell. To nobody else except you could I admit this. That you comprehend, I know. Furthermore, poor Herb—he—he cares for me and my love belongs to him, Nell. Nothing was meant to me by the others, yet he matters—and provided I could remain alive, I would become his wife and experience such happiness. Oh, Nell, this is difficult.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
